title: Lupus and RA Serology: Anti-Sm, Anti-dsDNA, Drug-Induced Lupus, RF and Anti-CCP
summary: Separate the specific-but-static anti-Sm from the activity-linked anti-dsDNA, recognise the anti-histone profile of classic drug-induced lupus and its anti-TNF exception, and explain why anti-CCP is more specific than rheumatoid factor for rheumatoid arthritis.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 53 Hits 1, 3 and 14 and Exam Traps 2 and 3. Checked against Fu 2015 and Pagkopoulou 2025 (anti-dsDNA), van Beers 2022 (anti-Sm), Dalle Vedove 2012 (drug-induced lupus), Taylor 2011 and Wu 2021 (RF and anti-CCP), all full text via Europe PMC. Qualified: Hit 1 “tracks activity” (the correlation is modest and serologically active, clinically quiescent patients exist; register flag rv-dsdna-activity-modest); Hit 14 “anti-dsDNA usually absent” (true for classic drugs, not for anti-TNF-induced lupus; rv-dil-anti-tnf-dsdna); Hit 3 figures are assay-, cutoff- and cohort-dependent (rv-ccp-rf-figures). Not taught: RF in 70% of Sjögren syndrome, RF 66–85% sensitivity/72% specificity, the 1940 and 2002 dates, ~15% seronegative RA, and antinucleosome/anti-ssDNA in drug-induced lupus.

objectives: Contrast anti-Sm (specific, not an activity marker) with anti-dsDNA (linked to activity, nephritis and low complement) and state the limits of anti-dsDNA monitoring.
Recognise the serological profile of classic drug-induced lupus and the anti-TNF-alpha exception.
Explain why anti-CCP is more specific than rheumatoid factor for rheumatoid arthritis and list common causes of a positive RF without RA.

scenes.title: Three positive results, three meanings
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach the immunology bench. (1) A woman with SLE three months into treatment: anti-dsDNA falling, C3 and C4 rising. (2) An 80-year-old with chronic hepatitis C and aching joints: rheumatoid factor weakly positive, anti-CCP negative. (3) A man on hydralazine for 3 years with arthritis and pleuritis: ANA positive, anti-histone positive, anti-dsDNA negative, complement normal. Question token: “What does each result really mean?”

cues.text: Three results reach the bench. A woman with lupus on treatment: her anti-double-stranded DNA is falling while C3 and C4 climb back.

An eighty-year-old with chronic hepatitis C and aching joints has a weakly positive rheumatoid factor but a negative anti-CCP. And a man on hydralazine for three years has arthritis, pleuritis and anti-histone antibodies, without anti-double-stranded DNA.
Each result is positive for something. What does each one really mean?

props.label: What does each result really mean?

scenes.title: The lupus pair: signature and dial
scenes.altText: Two cards. Anti-Sm: targets Sm core proteins of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (SmD1 and SmD3 the most SLE-specific); very specific for SLE; found in roughly 5–30% of patients depending on ethnicity and method; worth 6 points in the 2019 EULAR/ACR immunology domain; conflicting clinical associations, so not regarded as an activity or prognostic marker. Anti-dsDNA: in about 50–70% of SLE; high specificity; associated with lupus nephritis; levels can rise in flares and fall or disappear after immunosuppression; elevated anti-dsDNA with low C3/C4 is a surrogate for exacerbation. Caveat token: the activity correlation is modest.

cues.text: Two lupus antibodies, two different jobs. Anti-Sm targets the Sm core proteins of the small nuclear ribonucleoproteins that help splice RNA. It is very specific for lupus, but only about five to thirty percent of patients have it, depending on ethnicity and method.
In the 2019 EULAR and ACR classification criteria, anti-Sm carries six points in the immunology domain. But because its links to clinical features conflict, it is not used as an activity marker.

Anti-double-stranded DNA is found in about half to seventy percent of patients and is linked to lupus nephritis. Its level can rise in a flare and fall, or even disappear, after immunosuppression, and a high anti-DNA with low C3 and C4 is a classic sign of exacerbation.
One caution: the match between anti-DNA level and activity is modest. Some patients stay serologically active while clinically quiet, so trends are read with the clinical picture.

props.title: Anti-dsDNA = dial
lines: Rises in flares, falls on therapy

props.label: Correlation is modest: read trends with the clinic

scenes.title: When a drug causes the lupus
scenes.altText: Classic drug-induced lupus card (Dalle Vedove 2012): lupus-like illness after months to years of continuous drug exposure (hydralazine, procainamide, quinidine most often; also isoniazid, methyldopa, minocycline, chlorpromazine); arthritis and serositis; ANA over 99%, anti-histone up to 95%, anti-dsDNA under 5%, hypocomplementaemia under 1%; resolves within weeks of stopping the drug. Exception card: lupus with anti-TNF-alpha agents — anti-dsDNA in 70–90% and low complement in 59%, anti-histone less often (up to 57%). Note: anti-histone antibodies also occur in idiopathic SLE (about 30% in Pagkopoulou 2025; up to 50% in Dalle Vedove 2012).

cues.text: Classic drug-induced lupus follows months or years of continuous exposure to a drug, most often hydralazine, procainamide or quinidine. Arthritis and serositis are typical, and nearly every patient is ANA positive.

The antibody profile is narrow: anti-histone antibodies in up to ninety-five percent, but anti-double-stranded DNA in fewer than five percent, and complement is almost never low. Stop the drug, and the illness resolves within weeks.
Anti-histone is not proof on its own: it is also reported in about thirty percent, and in some series up to half, of patients with ordinary lupus.
And one exception breaks the rule. Lupus triggered by anti-TNF-alpha biologics often shows anti-double-stranded DNA, in seventy to ninety percent, with low complement in more than half.

scenes.title: Rheumatoid factor vs anti-CCP
scenes.altText: RF card: antibody against the Fc portion of IgG, mostly IgM in RA (60–80% of patients); also found in SLE, Sjögren disease, sarcoidosis, chronic infections (hepatitis B or C, infective endocarditis) and healthy people, rising with age (3–5% of healthy adults, 10–30% of the elderly). Anti-CCP card: anti-citrullinated protein antibodies, in about two-thirds of RA; in a meta-analysis of 56 studies anti-CCP2 had sensitivity 68% and specificity 95%, against 60% and 79% for RF in 29 studies; both are in the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria, with more points for high titre (over 3 times the upper limit of normal). Hook answers card.

cues.text: Rheumatoid factor is an antibody against the Fc tail of IgG, usually IgM. It is found in most people with established rheumatoid arthritis, but also in lupus, Sjögren disease, chronic infections such as hepatitis C, and in healthy older people.

Anti-CCP detects antibodies to citrullinated proteins, present in about two-thirds of patients. In pooled analyses, anti-CCP2 had sixty-eight percent sensitivity with ninety-five percent specificity across fifty-six studies; rheumatoid factor managed sixty and seventy-nine percent across twenty-nine. Both count in the 2010 criteria, with more points for a high titre.

Back to the hook. The woman with lupus: falling anti-DNA with recovering complement fits a treatment response. The eighty-year-old: a weak rheumatoid factor with hepatitis C and a negative anti-CCP may well be nonspecific.
The man on hydralazine: anti-histone without anti-DNA and normal complement fits classic drug-induced lupus, which should resolve once the drug is stopped.

props.title: Hook answers
lines: 2 Weak RF, CCP −, hepatitis C: nonspecific

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Anti-Sm and anti-dsDNA are interchangeable” (✓ anti-Sm is the specific signature but is not an activity marker; anti-dsDNA moves with activity, modestly); “RF positive = rheumatoid arthritis” (✓ RF occurs in other autoimmune diseases, chronic infections and healthy elderly; anti-CCP is more specific); “Positive anti-dsDNA rules out drug-induced lupus” (✓ true for classic drugs, but anti-TNF lupus is often anti-dsDNA positive).

cues.text: Trap one: anti-Sm and anti-DNA are interchangeable. No: anti-Sm is the specific signature but is not used to follow activity; anti-DNA is the one that moves.
Trap two: rheumatoid factor positive means rheumatoid arthritis. No: it appears in other autoimmune diseases, chronic infections and healthy older people. Anti-CCP is the more specific test.
Trap three: a positive anti-DNA rules out drug-induced lupus. Mostly true for classic drugs, but lupus from anti-TNF biologics is often anti-DNA positive.

props.title: ✗ “Anti-Sm = anti-dsDNA.”
lines: ✓ Sm: specific, not a monitor · dsDNA: moves with activity

props.title: ✗ “RF + = rheumatoid arthritis.”
lines: ✓ RF is nonspecific; anti-CCP is the specific test

scenes.title: Signature, dial, history, certificate
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Sm is the SIGNATURE — it identifies lupus but is not used to follow it. dsDNA is the DIAL — it turns with activity. Histone is the drug’s HISTORY — the classic drug-induced profile. CCP is the CERTIFICATE for rheumatoid arthritis; RF is a common RUMOUR.” Tokens for each. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: anti-Sm is the signature that identifies lupus, not a gauge to follow it. Anti-DNA is the dial that turns with activity. Anti-histone is the drug history. Anti-CCP is the certificate for rheumatoid arthritis, and rheumatoid factor is a common rumour.

Where it breaks: the anti-DNA dial is imprecise and some quiet patients keep high levels; anti-histone also occurs in ordinary lupus, and anti-TNF lupus has anti-DNA; and a small share of healthy people carry anti-CCP, while many patients with rheumatoid arthritis have none.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Anti-Sm = specific, not a monitor · anti-dsDNA + C3/C4 = activity (modest)”, “Classic drug lupus = anti-histone, no dsDNA · anti-CCP more specific than RF”.

cues.text: Anti-Sm is a specific lupus signature that is not used to track activity, anti-dsDNA with complement moves with lupus activity only modestly, classic drug-induced lupus shows anti-histone without anti-dsDNA, and anti-CCP is more specific for rheumatoid arthritis than rheumatoid factor.

props.label: Anti-Sm = specific, not a monitor · anti-dsDNA + C3/C4 = activity (modest)
Drug lupus = anti-histone, no dsDNA · anti-CCP ≫ RF for specificity

explanation.what: Plain language: in lupus, one antibody (anti-Sm) is like a name tag that says “lupus” but does not change with how sick the person is, while another (anti-dsDNA) tends to go up when the disease flares and down with treatment. Some medicines can cause a lupus-like illness with a different antibody pattern that goes away when the drug is stopped. For rheumatoid arthritis, the older test (rheumatoid factor) is often positive in other conditions and in healthy older people, while anti-CCP is much more specific. Scientific terms: anti-Smith (anti-Sm; SmD1/SmD3), small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (snRNP), anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), Crithidia luciliae immunofluorescence test (CLIFT), Farr assay, hypocomplementaemia (C3, C4), serologically active clinically quiescent SLE, drug-induced lupus erythematosus (DILE), anti-histone antibody, anti-TNF-alpha, rheumatoid factor (RF; anti-IgG Fc), anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA), anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP2), 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria.
explanation.why: Anti-Sm is very specific but its clinical associations are inconsistent, so it supports classification rather than monitoring. Anti-dsDNA participates in immune complexes that fix complement, so rising levels with falling C3/C4 can accompany flares, but the relationship is imperfect. In classic DILE the autoantibody response centres on histones and rarely includes anti-dsDNA. RF is part of normal immune responses to infection and immunisation and increases with age, which limits its specificity; ACPA reflects a response to citrullinated proteins that is far more confined to RA.
explanation.measure: Anti-Sm: ~5–30% of SLE (ethnicity- and method-dependent); 6 points in the 2019 EULAR/ACR immunology domain; gold standard immunoprecipitation, routine ELISA, line, bead, CLIA or FEIA assays. Anti-dsDNA: ~50–70% of SLE; CLIFT, Farr and ELISA correlate in populations but disagree in individuals; a surge predicted a severe flare with sensitivity 62%, specificity 80%, PPV 59% in one cohort cited by Fu 2015. Classic DILE: ANA >99%, anti-histone up to 95%, anti-dsDNA <5%, hypocomplementaemia <1%; anti-TNF DILE: anti-dsDNA 70–90%, hypocomplementaemia 59%. RF: 3–5% of healthy adults, 10–30% of the elderly; RF pooled sensitivity 60% and specificity 79% (29 studies). Anti-CCP2: sensitivity 68%, specificity 95% (56 studies); ACPA in 1–3% of healthy people, usually at low levels. 2010 criteria: high titre = over 3 times the upper limit of normal.
explanation.differs: Anti-Sm (specific, not an activity marker) vs anti-dsDNA (activity-linked, nephritis); idiopathic SLE (anti-dsDNA common, low complement) vs classic DILE (anti-histone, no anti-dsDNA, normal complement) vs anti-TNF DILE (anti-dsDNA common); RF (sensitive-ish, nonspecific) vs anti-CCP (similar or better sensitivity, much more specific).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: which antibody falls with treatment as C3/C4 recover (anti-dsDNA), which is most specific for SLE (anti-Sm), a procainamide or hydralazine patient with anti-histone and no anti-dsDNA (drug-induced lupus), and the most specific test for RA (anti-CCP) or a cause of false-positive RF.

right.label: Anti-dsDNA
points: Rises in flares, falls on therapy

mnemonic.text: Sm is the SIGNATURE (identifies lupus, not used to follow it); dsDNA is the DIAL (turns with activity); histone is the drug HISTORY (classic drug-induced lupus); CCP is the CERTIFICATE for rheumatoid arthritis, and RF is a common RUMOUR.
mnemonic.explanation: Links each antibody to its main exam role: specificity, activity, drug cause or RA specificity.
mnemonic.limitation: Anti-Sm is not shown to be unchanging, only unhelpful as an activity marker; the anti-dsDNA dial is imprecise and some clinically quiet patients keep high levels; anti-histone also occurs in idiopathic SLE and anti-TNF lupus often has anti-dsDNA; 1–3% of healthy people carry ACPA and about a third of RA patients lack it.

questions.stem: A woman with SLE and nephritis starts immunosuppressive therapy. Over three months her C3 and C4 return toward normal. Which antibody level is most likely to fall in parallel?

options.rationale: Correct. Anti-dsDNA levels can rise in flares and fall after immunosuppression, often alongside recovering complement, although the correlation with activity is modest.
Incorrect. Anti-Sm is very specific for SLE but is not regarded as an activity marker.
Incorrect. Anti-histone is the hallmark of classic drug-induced lupus and is not used to monitor SLE activity.
Incorrect. Anti-CCP is a rheumatoid arthritis antibody, not an SLE activity marker.

questions.stem: A man treated with hydralazine for 3 years develops arthritis and pleuritis. ANA and anti-histone antibodies are positive, anti-dsDNA is negative, and C3/C4 are normal. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Classic drug-induced lupus, expected to resolve within weeks of stopping the drug
options.rationale: Correct. Classic drug-induced lupus shows ANA and anti-histone antibodies, rarely anti-dsDNA or low complement, and resolves after the drug is stopped.
Incorrect. Idiopathic SLE commonly has anti-dsDNA and low complement; anti-histone alone with a drug history points to drug-induced lupus.
Incorrect. He is on hydralazine, not an anti-TNF biologic, and anti-TNF lupus often shows anti-dsDNA and low complement.

options.text: Rheumatoid arthritis, confirmed by the positive ANA
options.rationale: Incorrect. ANA is not a rheumatoid arthritis test; RF and anti-CCP are the RA serologies.

questions.stem: An 80-year-old with chronic hepatitis C and joint aches has a weakly positive rheumatoid factor and a negative anti-CCP. Which statement is best?

options.text: The RF may be nonspecific; chronic infection and older age both raise RF positivity, and anti-CCP is the more specific RA test
options.rationale: Correct. RF occurs in chronic infections such as hepatitis C and rises with age in healthy people; anti-CCP has much higher specificity.

options.text: A positive RF confirms rheumatoid arthritis
options.rationale: Incorrect. RF also occurs in other autoimmune diseases, chronic infections and healthy older people.

options.text: A negative anti-CCP excludes rheumatoid arthritis
options.rationale: Incorrect. Anti-CCP is present in only about two-thirds of patients, so a negative result does not exclude RA.

options.text: Anti-CCP is less specific than RF and should be ignored
options.rationale: Incorrect. Anti-CCP is more specific than RF (about 95% vs 79% in pooled studies).

claims.text: Anti-Sm: snRNP target, very specific for SLE, ~5–30% sensitivity, 6 points in the 2019 criteria, not an activity marker.
Anti-dsDNA: ~50–70% of SLE, nephritis link, rises in flares and falls after immunosuppression, with low C3/C4 a surrogate for exacerbation.
Correlation of anti-dsDNA with activity is modest; surge statistics; serologically active clinically quiescent SLE; assay discordance; no consensus to treat on serology alone.
Classic DILE: drugs, features, antibody profile (anti-histone up to 95%, anti-dsDNA <5%, normal complement), resolution after stopping; anti-histone also in idiopathic SLE (~30%, up to 50%).
RF targets IgG Fc (mostly IgM); also in SLE, Sjögren, sarcoidosis, chronic infections and healthy elderly (3–5% of adults, 10–30% of elderly).
ACPA in about two-thirds of RA; anti-CCP2 68%/95% vs RF 60%/79% in pooled studies; ACPA in 1–3% of healthy people; both in the 2010 criteria with high titre >3 × ULN.

Reviewer specifics: RF positive in 70% of Sjögren syndrome; RF 66–85% sensitivity and 72% specificity; anti-CCP “up to 98%” specificity as a general figure; 1940 and 2002 test dates; ~15% seronegative RA; antinucleosome and anti-ssDNA antibodies in drug-induced lupus.
claims.note: Not taught; not found or given differently in the sources read.

claims.text: Scenario invented; antibodies shown schematically as cards.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 53 Hit 1 (and Exam Trap 2) says anti-dsDNA tracks SLE disease activity and falls with treatment. Pagkopoulou 2025 agrees levels can rise in flares and fall after immunosuppression, but both it and Fu 2015 state the correlation with activity is modest or inconsistent: a surge predicted a severe flare with PPV 59% in one cohort, serologically active clinically quiescent patients are common, assays disagree in individual patients, and there is no consensus to treat on serology alone (register flag rv-dsdna-activity-modest).

Ch. 53 Hit 14 says anti-dsDNA is usually absent in drug-induced lupus. Dalle Vedove 2012 confirms this for classic DILE (<5%) but reports anti-dsDNA in 70–90% and hypocomplementaemia in 59% of anti-TNF-alpha-induced lupus (register flag rv-dil-anti-tnf-dsdna).

Ch. 53 Hit 3 gives anti-CCP2 up to 98% specificity with ~70% sensitivity and RF 66–85% sensitivity with 72% specificity. Taylor 2011 reports pooled anti-CCP2 sensitivity 68% and specificity 95% (56 studies), with individual-study specificities of 91.5–98.8% depending on cutoff and method, and RF 60%/79% (29 studies) or 62%/87% (>5,000 patients); Wu 2021 gives RF specificity of about 60–70%. The figures depend on assay, cutoff and comparator cohort (register flag rv-ccp-rf-figures).
